sections.note: Philosophies, Policies, and Programs for Veterans Description: This course explores the philosophies, policies, and government-supported programs that shape the care and services provided to military veterans. Students will examine the structure and function of the Department of Veterans Affairs, as well as key programs related to health, housing, employment, and education. Designed for social workers and public health professionals, the course emphasizes practical strategies for advocacy, ethical service delivery, and holistic support planning for veterans. sections.note: Explore how nonprofits address social issues while working as a class “mini foundation” to award tens of thousands of dollars in real grants. Research nonprofits, conduct site visits, debate where funding can make the greatest difference, and select recipients.

restrictions: Restricted to Chancellor's Scholar-CHPHonors students.
sections.note: Are you passionate about social issues like housing, mental health, or access to education? As a partner course of The Philanthropy Lab, students will work together as a class “mini foundation” to direct up to $85,000 in real grant funding to nonprofits of their choosing each term. As you learn about the nonprofit sector and the role it plays in addressing social issues, you’ll research nonprofits, conduct site visits, debate where funding can make the greatest difference, and work with selected recipients at an end-of-term Giving Ceremony. The nonprofit sector employs around 10% of the US workforce and plays an important role in addressing needs not fully met by business or government. Nonprofits provide essential services, strengthen communities, and enrich our lives through the arts. This course explores how the nonprofit sector works, the challenges it faces, and the role it plays in society, while giving you hands-on experience making real grantmaking decisions with real consequences. This course is approved for General Education Credit for Social Science.

sections.note: Telehealth & Clinical Social Work: Telehealth, mobile technology, and digital communication are gaining widespread use in social work direct practice and can increase access to mental and behavioral health care. This 8-week course covers types of telehealth, ethics, professional standards and etiquette, online therapy tools, clinical skills, evidence-based practices, and telehealth policies. The strengths and limitations of these evolving technologies will be reviewed, and best practices for access, equity, digital health literacy, and cultural competence will be considered throughout. The course will include presentations, readings/video assignments, case studies, role-playing, progress notes, hands-on skills training, and a final project. This is a 2-credit hour course. The class meets the 2nd 8 weeks of the semester.

sections.note: This course focuses on building students' skills in Motivational Interviewing, an evidence-based method for talking with people who are ambivalent about change. This course differentiates the counseling method from other counseling approaches and teaches students the practice theory upon which the counseling method is built. Ample time is devoted to practicing skills via role plays. Skills developed include reflective listening skills, formulation of questions, and directive methods that are distinct in MI. Special attention is devoted to applying Motivational Interviewing with diverse populations and across varied target problems.
